## Overview

**Condo Price Analysis in Cambodia** — part of the [Data Science Projects Collection](https://github.com/PaulChanCyber/Data-Science-Project-). ITC condo-for-sale study: price drivers, districts, and formal PDS project management.

## Background of the Study

This study examines **urban condo sales in Phnom Penh and other Cambodian cities** in Cambodia—a context where digital classifieds and e-commerce listings have accelerated price transparency but not necessarily price *understanding*. Stakeholders include investors, agents, and owner-occupiers. **Condo for Sale in Cambodia** — ITC AMS PDS 2022–2023 (Lecturer **CHAN Sophal**). Five-member group with formal project management sections in guideline. The project folder on GitHub contains notebooks, and in many cases a formal **Project Guideline** PDF that records the instructor-approved objectives, timeline, and evaluation plan. That document is the contract between the student team and the course: it states what will be delivered, which algorithms will be compared, and how success will be measured. The work was completed in the **Programming for Data Science (PDS)** course at the **Institute of Technology of Cambodia (ITC)**, Department of Applied Mathematics and Statistics, under instructor **CHAN Sophal**. Deliverables typically include a **Project Guideline** alignment document, Jupyter notebooks, visualizations, a written report, and presentation slides—mirroring how data analysts are expected to document real engagements for technical and non-technical audiences.

## Motivation of the Study

**Why this topic matters:** Condo units vary by floor, view, and district; structured analysis reveals where premiums concentrate. Condo investment in Phnom Penh and provincial cities requires comparables adjusted for district, floor, and amenities—often buried in unstructured listings. From an academic standpoint, **Condo Price Analysis in Cambodia** trains competencies employers list repeatedly: pandas data wrangling, visualization literacy, scikit-learn modeling, and clear written communication. From a practical standpoint, even a simple benchmark model helps investors, agents, and owner-occupiers negotiate fairer deals and spot overpriced listings. The motivation is therefore both **social** (fairer, more informed transactions) and **pedagogical** (evidence that the team followed the guideline, compared models fairly, and can explain limitations such as sample bias, missing data, and temporal drift).

## Project Guidelines & Objectives

The following objectives and steps are taken from the team's **Project Guideline** (see GitHub) and reflect how the instructor graded the capstone: **From *Project guideline: Condo for Sale in Cambodia*:**

- **Goal:** Analyze condo sale market—which units are most expensive and where; identify **price drivers**
- **Sections:** Objectives, scope, timeline, resources, risks/mitigation, approvals
- **Analytical flow:** EDA → modeling → conclusions aligned with condo-for-sale domain Teams were expected to show intermediate artifacts—not only a final accuracy number. That includes data dictionaries, plots defending modeling choices, and a short conclusion on which model to deploy or recommend for the stated business question.

## Data Collection & Preparation

Reliable conclusions depend on documenting **where data came from**, **how often it was collected**, and **what each column means**. For this project: Scraped condo sale listings across Cambodian markets (see team notebooks/reports). Typical preparation steps across PDS scraping projects include deduplicating listings, standardizing currencies (USD vs. KHR), parsing text fields (e.g., '3+ bedrooms'), handling missing values with explicit rules, and flagging extreme prices before modeling. Those steps reduce leakage and prevent a single erroneous row from dominating metrics.

## Methodology & Analysis

Analytical work proceeded in reproducible notebook stages so instructors could rerun cells during defense sessions: Clean listing fields; visualize price by district and unit attributes; regression or tree models for sale price; geographic breakdown of premium segments. Where applicable, teams compared multiple algorithms rather than reporting a single default model. Feature engineering was justified with plots (distributions, correlations, geographic breakdowns) so stakeholders could see *why* variables entered the model—not only *that* they improved error metrics.

## Model Evaluation

Model evaluation followed train/validation/test discipline taught in PDS: Model error on hold-out listings; map/visual summary of expensive districts. Beyond scalar error, teams were encouraged to inspect **residuals** (regression), **confusion matrices** (classification), or **forecast overlays** (time series) to detect systematic bias—such as underpricing premium districts or overfitting rare categories.

## Results & Key Learnings

Investor-oriented view of condo price drivers and top-tier districts. Completing **Condo Price Analysis in Cambodia** provides evidence of end-to-end data science execution: from raw scrape to defended conclusions. For portfolio readers, the GitHub repository contains the artifacts to verify claims—notebooks, and in many folders, slide decks and PDF reports. Limitations are worth stating explicitly: scraped data snapshots age quickly; models trained in 2022–2023 may need retraining as market conditions shift. That honesty is part of professional practice.
